Two large USGS 3DEP lidar datasets were also added over southern California. This month's release brings new coverage across Europe, Central America, and the US. High-resolution, country-wide digital elevation models covering Norway, Finland, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein were added, offering national bare-earth and surface terrain coverage at 0.5–2 meter resolution. Numerous UAV-derived surveys over Guatemala were also contributed to OpenTopography's Community Dataspace program. In the US, several new USGS 3DEP lidar datasets were added in Arkansas, along with a NOAA-provided dataset over parts of Virginia.

New datasets were added in June 2026 spanning the US mainland, Alaska, and two continental to global-scale digital terrain models (DTMs). ANADEM is a machine learning-derived DTM covering all of South America, while GEDTM is a near-global-scale DTM. This month's additions also include two lidar surveys in California, USGS 3DEP lidar datasets in Alabama, Arkansas, Idaho, and Alaska, and a Community Dataspace dataset over southwestern Virginia.

New Machine Learning Derived Digital Terrain Models

OpenTopography is pleased to announce the availability of two new continental to global-scale digital terrain models (DTMs): ANADEM, covering South America, and the Global Ensemble Digital Terrain Model (GEDTM), covering nearly all global landmasses. Both datasets represent a significant advance in the ability to characterize bare-earth terrain from existing Digital Surface Models.
A Digital Terrain Model (DTM) of a section of the Congo River basin. The DTM is colored by elevation and draped on a hillshade generated from the Global Ensemble Digital Terrain Model (GEDTM).
Upgraded Hydrologic Analysis Tools Now Available

For the past decade OpenTopography has offered on-demand tools for hydrologic processing of topography. These tools enable hydrologically conditioning of DEMs, calculation of contributing area and flow paths, and topographic wetness index. OpenTopography has recently updated our hydrologic routing service with a new toolset built on Whitebox Workflows (WbW). A lidar survey over the San Juan Mountains in Colorado was added, as well as many 3DEP lidar datasets in Vermont, California, Oregon, and Alaska. A Community Dataspace dataset over the Stromboli Volcano in Italy was also shared with the community.

New USGS 3DEP datasets in Nevada, Ohio, and Oregon, along with Community Dataspace datasets from China, Virginia, and Iceland are also now available.

New USGS 3DEP datasets in California and Nevada and NOAA Coastal lidar data from the Ozarks region and Oregon further expand coverage across diverse environments.

OpenTopography's Spring 2026 Webinar Series
OpenTopography invites you to join a series of weekly, hour-long webinars in March and April 2026.

The first webinar introduces OpenTopography and our new resources and should be of interest to all. The three subsequent webinars are aimed at those with some familiarity with lidar who are seeking to make better use of these data in their research and teaching.
If you are looking for webinars that more broadly introduce high-resolution topography, please review our past webinar series from 2023 and 2025.
Webinars are free to attend, but advance registration is required.
